summary: CI/CD and persistent cloud sandboxes that share one reproducible build runtime.
editor_note: Agent sandboxes and CI belong in the same execution graph rather than two drifting environments. Content-addressed filesystem layers, automatic cache hits, one VM per task, and SSH breakpoints make build state inspectable. Uncommitted changes can run the same validation before a push, while secrets enter individual tasks without appearing in the agent prompt. The question is whether those gains survive complex monorepos and long-lived stateful services.
tags: ci cd,developer tools,agent sandboxes,build caching,cloud runtimes

product_evidence.claim: RWX runs each task in its own virtual machine and executes dependency graphs in parallel with automatic content-based caching.
Agent sandboxes reuse the CI runtime and configuration, snapshot content-addressed filesystem layers, and keep processes warm across iterations.

market_context.primary_user: Software teams that want coding agents and human contributors to validate changes in reproducible cloud build environments.
market_context.differentiation: The same task graph, cache, and secret model powers pre-push agent sandboxes and CI instead of maintaining separate execution stacks.
market_context.why_now: The August 2026 Series A follows rising agent-generated code volume, which increases the cost of slow or inconsistent validation.

risks.claim: Whether shared runtimes reduce end-to-end build time and migration work can be tested on large monorepos with stateful integration services.
risks.basis: The official pages document caching and snapshots, but do not publish independent migration or workload-level benchmarks.
